seo_title: How to Choose a Wedding Videographer | Zen Visuals
seo_description: A plain guide to choosing a wedding videographer: what to watch for in their films, the questions to ask, what a fair price looks like and the red flags. By Zen Visuals.
h1: How to choose a wedding videographer
hero_alt: Bride and groom walking hand in hand across a lawn above the valley
intro: Your wedding film is the one thing from the day that you'll watch again and again, and the one thing you can't redo. Choosing who makes it matters more than almost any other supplier. This is how we'd choose, if it were our wedding.
We're Zuzia and Ben of Zen Visuals, wedding videographers in Derbyshire. We've written this to be useful whoever you book.

sections.heading: Watch three full films, not just highlights
sections.text: A ninety-second showreel shows anyone's best shots. Ask for three complete wedding films from the last year and watch them to the end. Do the films hold your attention? Can you hear the vows and the speeches clearly? Does the colour look natural, with skin tones that look like skin? Does each film feel like a different couple, or the same template?

sections.heading: Ask who will actually be there
sections.text: Some companies send whoever is free. Ask who will film your wedding, whether it's the person you've spoken to, and whether there'll be one camera or two. Two people means the ceremony and speeches are covered from more than one angle, and someone is always on the couple.

sections.heading: Ask what the price covers
sections.text: Compare the length of coverage, the length of the finished film, whether the full ceremony and speeches are included or an extra, how the music is licensed, and how long the edit takes. A low price for six hours can cost more once you've added the evening.

sections.heading: Ask how long you'll wait
sections.text: Three to six weeks is reasonable for a highlights film. Six months is not unusual in the industry, and it's worth knowing before you book.

sections.heading: Check they'll work well with your photographer
sections.text: Ask how they share space with the photographer during portraits and the ceremony. The best answer is that they plan it together on the day and never block each other's shot.

sections.heading: Read the reviews for specifics
sections.text: Five stars are easy. Look for reviews that mention the videographer by name and say something specific: that guests didn't notice them, that the vows were clear, that the film made them cry. Google reviews are harder to fake than testimonials on a website.

sections.heading: Red flags
sections.text: Won't show full films. Vague about who's filming. A contract with no delivery date. Big discounts for booking today. Films where the audio is only music and you never hear the couple.

sections.heading: What we do
sections.text: For the record: we show you full films, it's always the two of us, every price covers your whole day, your film is ready within 3 to 6 weeks, and the full ceremony and speeches can be added as their own films.

faqs.question: How much should a wedding videographer cost?
faqs.answer: In Derbyshire, whole-day coverage with an edited highlights film commonly runs from around £1,000 to £2,500, depending on the number of people filming, the length of the film and what's included. Ours is £1,100 for the whole day.

faqs.question: Is a wedding videographer worth it?
faqs.answer: Photographs show how the day looked. A film shows how it sounded and felt: the vows, the speeches, the laughter. Most couples who have one say it's the thing they return to most.

faqs.question: How long should a wedding film be?
faqs.answer: Highlights films are usually three to six minutes, long enough to tell the story and short enough to watch often. Full ceremony and speech films run as long as the events themselves.

faqs.question: When should we book a videographer?
faqs.answer: Good videographers book up a year or more ahead for summer Saturdays. Once you have a venue and a date, book the photographer and videographer next.
